what: CoreWeave rents out computing power for artificial intelligence. It builds data centres filled with graphics processors and leases that capacity to AI labs and enterprises under multi-year contracts.
customers: AI research labs, large technology companies and enterprises training and running AI models.
money: GPU capacity, storage and networking sold under contract
moat: Data centre capacity and GPU supply secured ahead of a shortage, with software tuned for large training clusters that general-purpose clouds were not built for.
risks: Debt of about $66 billion funds data centre and equipment purchases, an enormous figure
It makes a large net loss while building out capacity
A handful of customers account for most of its contracted revenue
GPUs depreciate quickly and the contracts must repay them before they do
opportunities: A contracted backlog stretching years out gives revenue visibility
Analysts see large upside, with a median target well above the current price
watch: Contracted backlog, customer concentration, and how new capacity is financed.
